extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academics acting as peer reviewers/referees for F1000Research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for conducting and submitting open, signed peer reviews of manuscripts submitted to F1000Research, including pre-acceptance checks, criteria to judge scientific soundness and reproducibility, recommended report structure, and recommended tone and transparency disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting to review: expertise and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm you have the appropriate expertise to assess the manuscript and that you can meet the required timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept if you lack the necessary subject-matter knowledge or the methods/statistics expertise to assess the work. If you cannot complete the review within the requested deadline, decline or propose an alternative timetable. If unsure about fit, explain limitations when submitting your response to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before accepting to review: competing interests and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for any competing interests (financial, professional, personal) or confidential relationships that would bias your review or prevent impartial assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline if you have a current collaboration or close personal relationship with the authors, are from the same institution, have a direct financial interest, or other conflicts that could bias the review. If a potential competing interest exists but is minor, disclose it to the editor and include it in your published review as required by the journal's policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and constructiveness of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Write reviews that are polite, constructive, objective and focused on the work rather than the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use respectful language; avoid ad hominem remarks. Provide actionable suggestions for improvement, explain why something is a problem, and, where possible, propose specific remedies or experiments. Remember that reviews are published and signed under F1000Research's open-peer-review model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the review report
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize your review into clear sections: a brief summary, major issues, minor issues, and a clear recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a concise summary of the study and its main findings. Separate major (critical) concerns from minor (editorial/clarity) points. Use line, figure, or section numbers when making specific comments. End with an explicit recommendation for the editor (e.g., approve/approve with reservations/not approved) and a brief justification tying comments to that recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation categories and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear published recommendation about the suitability of the article for publication and justify it with evidence from your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal's defined recommendation options (e.g., approve, approve with reservations, not approved) and explain how the manuscript meets or fails to meet scientific-soundness and transparency standards. Tie the decision directly to the major issues you raised so authors and readers can see the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific soundness / validity of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the study design, methods and analyses are appropriate to support the stated conclusions and whether the results are presented accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate experimental design, controls, reproducibility, adequacy of experimental groups/samples, potential biases, and whether conclusions overreach the data. Point out specific methodological flaws or unsupported inferences with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: data, code and materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the authors have made, or commit to making, underlying data, code, and materials available in accordance with the journal's policies so others can reproduce the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require data deposition in appropriate repositories, provide accession numbers/DOIs, ensure code and workflows are accessible (with versions and dependencies), and ask for clear links/instructions to reproduce analyses. If data cannot be shared, request justification and appropriate metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods detail and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure methods are described in sufficient detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments or analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for detailed descriptions of protocols, reagents (with supplier and catalog numbers), equipment models/settings, software names and versions, parameters, and step-by-step procedures. If key details are missing, request that authors expand the Methods or provide protocols as supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether statistical methods are appropriate, correctly applied, and adequately reported (including sample size justification, assumptions, multiple testing corrections, and effect sizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that tests used match data distributions, that p-values, confidence intervals, and effect sizes are reported where appropriate, and that sample size/power considerations are addressed. Request reanalysis or additional tests if current analyses are inadequate or misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results presentation and support for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the results presented (figures, tables, statistical summaries) support the authors' conclusions and that claims are not overstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure results are presented clearly, that key findings are supported by the data shown, and point out where conclusions exceed what the results justify. Suggest rewording of conclusions or additional analyses/controls where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures, tables and legends clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether figures and tables are clear, correctly labelled, and accompanied by informative legends that allow interpretation without referring back to the main text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check axis labels, units, sample sizes, error bar definitions, statistical annotations, and whether raw data or source files are available. Request higher-resolution images, clearer labels, or reformatting if graphics are ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, approvals and participant consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that studies involving humans, human data, animals or hazardous materials include statements of ethical approval and informed consent or appropriate animal welfare oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for ethics committee names and approval numbers, informed consent statements, clinical trial registration numbers (where applicable), and clear reporting of adherence to ethical standards. If approvals are missing or inadequate, request documentation or clarification and flag serious ethical concerns to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials and patient-safety reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For clinical research, check proper trial registration, reporting of harms/adverse events, and adherence to relevant reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure trial registration is reported with identifier, that methods and outcomes match the registry where appropriate, and that adverse events and safety monitoring are adequately described. Recommend adherence to appropriate reporting standards and request supplementary material as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, significance and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on the importance and potential impact of the findings for the field, while recognizing F1000Research's emphasis on scientific soundness over novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the work advances knowledge or provides useful data/resources. Do not reject solely for lack of novelty; focus on whether the study is robustly conducted and provides value (e.g., data sets, negative results, replication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship, contributorship and ethical publishing concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Note any concerns about authorship attribution, contributorship statements, undisclosed conflicts among authors, duplicate publication, or plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for clear contributorship statements and disclosures. If you suspect plagiarism or redundant publication, report these concerns confidentially to the editor with supporting evidence rather than making accusations in the public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting standards and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript follows relevant reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA, ARRIVE) and journal-specific policies for the article type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request completion of appropriate checklists or inclusion of missing items, and suggest authors include standardized reporting elements (flow diagrams, checklists, full protocols) as supplementary material where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational reproducibility and software reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For computational studies, ensure code, software versions, parameters, workflows, and containerization/virtual environments are reported to enable reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require access to source code (or a DOI for archived code), a description of computing environment, sample input and output, and preferably a workflow or container (e.g., Docker/Singularity) to reproduce analyses. Highlight missing details or inaccessible resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor issues: language, formatting and editorial corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out typos, unclear phrasing, grammatical issues, small formatting problems, and suggestions to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List line- or page-specific minor edits; suggest rewordings for clarity. Indicate if English language editing is needed but avoid making minor copyediting the main focus if major scientific concerns exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the review itself (competing interests and signed review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose any competing interests in your review and be aware that, under F1000Research policy, reviews are published and typically signed by the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear statement of competing interests in the review text. Do not include confidential material in the published review; if you need to communicate confidential concerns, raise them privately to the editor in addition to any public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments or analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for additional work only when necessary to support the conclusions, and distinguish between essential experiments and suggested extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate mandatory experiments/analyses that must be done to validate conclusions from optional suggestions that would strengthen but are not required. Provide guidance on feasible scope and realistic expectations for revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision justification and mapping comments to recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear mapping between the major issues you raised and your final recommendation so authors and editors understand the basis for your decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the key flaws or strengths that determine your recommendation, and indicate which issues are fatal to publication versus those that can be addressed in revision.
